h1: Fencing in Irving, TX: Wood, Iron, Repair and Gate Quotes
heroSub: From older south Irving streets to Las Colinas, Irving fence jobs start with the same question: what does the City of Irving require? Get two or three written quotes from independent fence contractors.
introHtml:
Fencing in Irving covers a lot of ground, because the city sits west of Dallas between downtown and DFW Airport and runs from older south Irving streets to the Las Colinas side. The calls are familiar: a 15-20 year old wood fence that has gone grey and started to lean, a section down after a spring storm, a driveway gate that stopped opening, or a new buyer who wants privacy or an iron front fence. This site is advertising for independent fence contractors. It does not build, repair or install anything itself.

Irving has one rule that catches homeowners out. The city's fence handout says any new or replacement fence needs a permit, and that a contractor, if you use one, must be registered in the City of Irving. Call (214) 555-0137 now, say which part of Irving the fence is in, and ask for comparable written quotes so you can compare them line by line.

services.title: Wood privacy fence installation
services.desc: Cedar or pine privacy fencing for Irving back yards, including board-on-board. The city's handout puts rear and side yards at 8 feet, so ask each contractor to quote the height you actually want in writing.

services.title: Fence repair
services.desc: Leaning posts, missing pickets and storm-damaged sections. Ask the contractor and the City where a repair ends and a replacement begins, because Irving's handout says replacement fences need a permit.

services.title: Gate repair and automatic gates
services.desc: Sagging walk gates, failed latches and driveway gates that stopped opening. Power wiring for an opener is electrical work, so ask the installer who holds the electrical licence.

services.title: Wrought iron fences
services.desc: Iron and steel fencing for front and rear yards. Irving's front-yard limit is 48 inches with at least 50 percent see-through, and an open picket style is one way to meet that.

sections.heading: What the City of Irving requires before a fence goes up
sections.html:
The City of Irving's "Fence Requirements" handout (updated 10/21/2020, excerpting Ordinance 2018-10044) says any new fence or replacement fence requires a permit. If a contractor is used, that contractor must be registered in the City of Irving. The handout is the version that could be read, a copy hosted by a fence firm, so confirm the current rules with the City's Inspections Department before you sign anything.

The same handout sets out the heights and the sight rules:

  • Front yards: not over 48 inches, with at least 50 percent through-visibility.
  • Rear and side yards: not over 8 feet in a residential zoning district.
  • Sight-easement and traffic-hazard rules apply, which matters most on a corner lot.

The handout says the permit fee follows the city's fee schedule, so ask each contractor what the permit costs and who pays it. Texas does not license fence contractors at the state level, but Irving asks for registration, so request the contractor's City of Irving registration and proof of insurance, and check both rather than taking them on trust. Your HOA, if you have one, is a separate approval. For comparison, Dallas starts requiring a permit above 6 feet in most yards; see fence installation in Dallas.

sections.heading: What fencing costs around Irving, and who says so
sections.html:
No Irving-specific fence price could be sourced, so these are Dallas-Fort Worth figures, each from one firm. TX Fence & Deck (Wylie, TX) wrote in May 2026 that installed cedar privacy fence in DFW runs $18 to $28 per linear foot at 6 feet. DFW Fence Contractor wrote in October 2025 of roughly $30 to $60 per linear foot for a standard 6-foot wood privacy fence. Those two disagree widely, which is the point: wood, style and contractor move the number more than the address does.

  • Board-on-board: TX Fence & Deck says it typically adds $2 to $5 per linear foot over a basic dog-ear fence.
  • Repair: Roof Raiders & Co (Dallas) advertises board replacement at $25 to $60 per board installed, and a full panel rebuild after wind (20 to 50 feet) at $1,200 to $3,500.
  • Gates: TX Fence & Deck says gate problems caught early cost $100 to $300 to fix, with motor replacements running $1,000 or more.
  • Iron: TX Fence & Deck advertises standard tubular steel residential fence at $30 to $45 per linear foot installed.

These are what individual firms advertise, not quotes from this site. Ask every contractor to price the same height, the same wood, the same footage and the same extras, such as haul-away of the old fence and the permit. More detail sits on the fence cost in Dallas page.

sections.heading: Storms, clay soil, HOAs and the neighbor on the other side
sections.html:
North Texas storms with 58 mph winds count as severe, according to the National Weather Service in Fort Worth, and a long solid fence takes the full push. After a storm, photograph the damage before anything moves, and get the gap closed first if a dog uses the yard. Then still get more than one written quote, because storm week is when rushed jobs happen. See fence repair for what to compare.

Much of the Dallas-Fort Worth area sits on expansive clay that swells and shrinks with moisture, per TxDOT-funded research from UT Arlington and the Texas A&M Transportation Institute (2008). It is fair to ask each contractor how they set posts in it and to get that in writing; no reliable post depth could be sourced, so none is given here. Texas law requires 811 to be called two business days before digging, and Texas811 says that when you hire a contractor, calling is the contractor's responsibility.

On HOAs, Texas Property Code Sec. 202.023 stops an association from banning perimeter fences outright, but it can still regulate the type of fencing, so get written approval before work starts. Whether a given street has an HOA depends on the street, so check yours. If your fence straddles the line and both of you use it, TexasLawHelp says both neighbors own it and share repair and replacement cost. That is general information, not legal advice.

faq.q: Do I need a permit to replace a fence in Irving?
faq.a: According to the City of Irving's Fence Requirements handout (updated October 2020), any new fence or replacement fence requires a permit. The handout also says a contractor, if used, must be registered in the City of Irving. Confirm the current rules with the City and your HOA before work starts.

faq.q: How tall can my fence be in Irving?
faq.a: The city handout lists rear and side yards at no more than 8 feet in a residential zoning district. Front yards are limited to 48 inches with at least 50 percent through-visibility. Sight-easement and traffic-hazard rules also apply, and an HOA can be stricter, so check with the City and your HOA.

faq.q: Does a fence contractor need a state licence to work in Irving?
faq.a: Texas does not license fence contractors at the state level, but Irving requires contractors to be registered with the City. Ask for the contractor's City of Irving registration and proof of insurance, and verify them with the City. This site does not vouch for any contractor's status.

faq.q: My driveway gate in Irving stopped opening. What might it cost to fix?
faq.a: TX Fence & Deck says gate issues caught early cost $100 to $300 to fix, and motor replacements run $1,000 or more. That is one DFW firm's advertised range, not a quote. Power wiring for an opener is electrical work, so ask the installer who holds the electrical licence, and call for gate repair quotes at (214) 555-0137.
